recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-29259 unless BR&R later chooses a broader editorial restructuring of ResearchSubject narrative.
issue_request: FHIR-29259 was Published with resolution Persuasive with Modification for R5. It asked BR&R to replace the ResearchSubject content definition and Scope and Usage text with language defining a ResearchSubject as a participant or object receiving investigative activities, clarifying possible subject types, privacy wording, the human-drug-trial note, and intended use cases.
initial_application: Git commit 5beb3e3941b0722af5ab73da66079646fd2a4631 explicitly applied J#29259 by changing source/researchsubject/structuredefinition-ResearchSubject.xml and source/researchsubject/researchsubject-introduction.xml. The current source still contains the requested StructureDefinition description/root definition and scope/use-case narrative.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists ResearchSubject as an active build-scoped resource under BR&R. BR&R minutes from 2023-01-03 approve FHIR-29259 using the Jira proposed language and resolution description with an 11-0-0 vote, and 2023-01-31 minutes list FHIR-29259 among completed ResearchSubject tickets. Later ResearchSubject introduction edits expanded participant terminology, retrospective-study subjects, and state/milestone guidance without reversing the FHIR-29259 text. FHIR-31768 was co-applied in the same historical commit but concerns separate consent cardinality and is already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was made because the current ResearchSubject source already conveys the approved FHIR-29259 definition and scope intent, and the later additions are compatible rather than conflicting.

related_jiras.note: The same 2023 implementation commit also changed ResearchSubject.consent cardinality for this separate issue; it is already represented on the combined branch and was not decided here.
Later ResearchSubject introduction improvements added participant terminology and retrospective-study context while preserving the FHIR-29259 definition and scope language.
